title: Insektmobilen - National citizen science and DNA metabarcoding survey of flying insects in June 2018 and 2019
description:
The Insectmobile (Insektmobilen) is a research project at the National History Museum of Denmark, University of Copenhagen, with the goal to investigate the diversity of flying insects in Denmark. In the summer of 2018, 2019 and 2020 almost 400 volunteers collected flying insects using large custom made insect nets mounted on the roof of their cars. The bulk insect samples were processed with a non-destructive DNA extraction DNA metabarcoding protocol (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmunk6ve) and sequences were assigned taxonomy by importing the fasta file into GBIF's sequence ID tool (https://www.gbif.org/tools/sequence-id). The sequences were queried against a 99% clustered version of the BOLD Public Database v2024-01-06 public data (COI-5P sequences).

The dataset contains unidentified sequences and potential errors and contaminants. For example, even though the primers used were developed as universal primers targeting freshwater insects, you will find other phyla, classes etc. We share these sequences and associated data for the data to be as open as possible, but please do reannotate sequences and filter the data for your specific needs prior to using the data for analysis. Please be aware that the samples may contain gut content of sampled insects and eDNA.

Sequence identification certainty is captured in the identificationRemarks field. The bit score is the required size of a sequence database in which the current match could be found just by chance. The bit score is a log2 scaled and normalized raw score. Each increase by one doubles the required database size (2bit-score). The expect value is a parameter that describes the number of hits one can "expect" to see by chance when searching a database of a particular size. It decreases exponentially as the score of the match increases. Hence, a low expect value is better. How much of the query(input) sequence aligns with the match in the the reference database, in percent. Badges representing different identity thresholds (match types); Blast exact match = identity >= 99% and queryCoverage >= 80%. This is within the threshold of the OTU, Blast ambiguous match = identity >= 99% and queryCoverage >= 80%, but there is at least one more match with similar identity, Blast close match = identity < 99% but > 90% and queryCoverage >= 80%. It is something close to the OTU, maybe the same genus, Blast weak match = there is a match, but with identity < 90% or/and queryCoverage < 80%. Depending on the quality of the sequence, bit score, identity and expect value, a higher taxon could be inferred from this, Blast no match = no match to the reference database.

fields.name: eventID
fields.title: Event ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: eventCategory
fields.title: Event Category
fields.description: A broad category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a limited, tightly controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: datasetName
fields.title: Dataset Name
fields.description: A name of a source dataset.
fields.rdfs:comment: The name identifying the data set from which the record was derived.

fields.name: eventConductedBy
fields.title: Event Conducted By
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of names of dcterms:Agents responsible for conducting or recording a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `José E. Crespo`; `Oliver P. Pearson | Anita K. Pearson`; `FMNH`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of names of people, groups, or organizations responsible for recording the original dwc:Occurrence. The primary collector or observer, especially one who applies a personal identifier (dwc:recordNumber), should be listed first.

fields.name: eventDate
fields.title: Event Date
fields.description: A date-time or time interval during which a dwc:Event occurred.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019. Not suitable for a time in a geological context.
fields.examples: `1963-03-08T14:07-06:00` (8 Mar 1963 at or after 2:07pm and before 2:08pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC); `2009-02-20T08:40Z` (20 February 2009 at or after 8:40am and before 8:41 UTC); `2018-08-29T15:19` (29 August 2018 at or after 3:19pm and before 3:20pm local time); `1809-02-12` (within the day 12 February 1809); `1906-06` (in the month of June 1906); `1971` (in the year 1971); `2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z` (some time within the interval beginning 1 March 2007 at 1pm UTC and before 11 May 2008 at 3:30pm UTC); `1900/1909` (some time within the interval between the beginning of the year 1900 and before the year 1909); `2007-11-13/15` (some time in the interval between the beginning of 13 November 2007 and before 15 November 2007)
fields.rdfs:comment: The date-time or interval during which a dwc:Event occurred. For occurrences, this is the date-time when the dwc:Event was recorded. Not suitable for a time in a geological context.

fields.name: habitat
fields.title: Habitat
fields.description: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.
fields.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.

fields.name: eventEffort
fields.title: Event Effort
fields.description: An amount of effort expended during a dwc:Event.
fields.examples: `40 trap-nights`; `10 observer-hours`; `10 km by foot`; `30 km by car`
fields.rdfs:comment: The amount of effort expended during a dwc:Event.

fields.name: eventRemarks
fields.title: Event Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Event.
fields.examples: `After the recent rains the river is nearly at flood stage.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Comments or notes about the dwc:Event.

fields.name: locationID
fields.title: Location ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of dcterms:Location information. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: country
fields.title: Country
fields.description: The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the dcterms:Location occurs.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names. Recommended best practice is to leave this field blank if the dcterms:Location spans multiple entities at this administrative level or if the dcterms:Location might be in one or another of multiple possible entities at this level. Multiplicity and uncertainty of the geographic entity can be captured either in the term dwc:higherGeography or in the term dwc:locality, or both.
fields.rdfs:comment: The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the dcterms:Location occurs.

fields.name: countryCode
fields.title: Country Code
fields.description: The standard code for the country in which the dcterms:Location occurs.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 country code, or 'ZZ' (for an unknown location or a location unassignable to a single country code), or 'XZ' (for the high seas beyond national jurisdictions). Multiplicity and uncertainty of the geographic entity can be captured either in the term dwc:higherGeography or in the term dwc:locality, or both.
fields.rdfs:comment: The standard code for the country in which the dcterms:Location occurs.

fields.name: locality
fields.title: Locality
fields.description: The specific description of the place.
fields.comments: Less specific geographic information can be provided in other geographic terms (dwc:higherGeography, dwc:continent, dwc:country, dwc:stateProvince, dwc:county, dwc:municipality, dwc:waterBody, dwc:island, dwc:islandGroup). This term may contain information modified from the original to correct perceived errors or standardize the description.
fields.examples: `Bariloche, 25 km NNE via Ruta Nacional 40 (=Ruta 237)`; `Queets Rainforest, Olympic National Park`
fields.rdfs:comment: The specific description of the place.

fields.name: decimalLatitude
fields.title: Decimal Latitude
fields.description: A geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. Valid values lie between -90 and 90, inclusive.
fields.rdfs:comment: The geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a dcterms:Location. Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. Legal values lie between -90 and 90, inclusive.

fields.name: decimalLongitude
fields.title: Decimal Longitude
fields.description: A geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. Valid values lie between -180 and 180, inclusive.
fields.rdfs:comment: The geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a dcterms:Location. Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. Legal values lie between -180 and 180, inclusive.

fields.name: geodeticDatum
fields.title: Geodetic Datum
fields.description: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude are based.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use the value `not recorded`. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for a string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude are based.

fields.name: coordinateUncertaintyInMeters
fields.title: Coordinate Uncertainty In Meters
fields.description: A horizontal distance (in meters) from a given dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the dcterms:Location. Zero is not a valid value for this term.
fields.comments: Leave the value empty if the uncertainty is unknown, cannot be estimated, or is not applicable (because there are no coordinates).
fields.examples: `30` (reasonable lower limit on or after 2000-05-01 of a GPS reading under good conditions if the actual precision was not recorded at the time); `100` (reasonable lower limit before 2000-05-01 of a GPS reading under good conditions if the actual precision was not recorded at the time); `71` (uncertainty for a UTM coordinate having 100 meter precision and a known spatial reference system)
fields.rdfs:comment: The horizontal distance (in meters) from the given dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the dcterms:Location. Leave the value empty if the uncertainty is unknown, cannot be estimated, or is not applicable (because there are no coordinates). Zero is not a valid value for this term.

fields.name: footprintWKT
fields.title: Footprint WKT
fields.description: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: A dcterms:Location may have both a point-radius representation (see dwc:decimalLatitude) and a footprint representation, and they may differ from each other.
fields.examples: `POLYGON ((10 20, 11 20, 11 21, 10 21, 10 20))` (the one-degree bounding box with opposite corners at longitude=10, latitude=20 and longitude=11, latitude=21)
fields.rdfs:comment: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines the dcterms:Location. A dcterms:Location may have both a point-radius representation (see dwc:decimalLatitude) and a footprint representation, and they may differ from each other.

fields.name: footprintSRS
fields.title: Footprint SRS
fields.description: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geometry given in dwc:footprintWKT is based.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use the value `not recorded`. It is also permitted to provide the SRS in Well-Known-Text, especially if no EPSG code provides the necessary values for the attributes of the SRS. Do not use this term to describe the SRS of the dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude, nor of any verbatim coordinates - use the dwc:geodeticDatum and dwc:verbatimSRS instead. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `EPSG:4326`; `GEOGCS["GCS_WGS_1984", DATUM["D_WGS_1984", SPHEROID["WGS_1984",6378137,298.257223563]], PRIMEM["Greenwich",0], UNIT["Degree",0.0174532925199433]]` (WKT for the standard WGS84 Spatial Reference System EPSG:4326); `not recorded`
fields.rdfs:comment: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geometry given in dwc:footprintWKT is based.

fields.name: preferredSpatialRepresentation
fields.title: Preferred Spatial Representation
fields.description: An indication of which spatial representation best represents the dcterms:Location.

fields.name: informationWithheld
fields.title: Information Withheld
fields.description: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
fields.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `location information not given for endangered species`; `collector identities withheld | ask about tissue samples`
fields.rdfs:comment: Additional information that exists, but that has not been shared in the given record.

fields.name: identificationID
fields.title: Identification ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Identification.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the dwc:Identification (the body of information associated with the assignment of a scientific name). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: materialEntityID
fields.title: Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity based on which a dwc:Identification was made.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: nucleotideSequenceID
fields.title: Nucleotide Sequence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:NucleotideSequence based on which a dwc:Identification was made.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: isAcceptedIdentification
fields.title: Is Accepted Identification
fields.description: An indicator that this dwc:Identification of a dwc:Organism is a currently an accepted or preferred one.

fields.name: taxonAssignmentMethod
fields.title: Taxon Assignment Method
fields.description: Tool and thresholds used to compare sequences when computing 'species-level' OTUs.

fields.name: identificationRemarks
fields.title: Identification Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Identification.
fields.examples: `Distinguished between Anthus correndera and Anthus hellmayri based on the comparative lengths of the uñas.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Comments or notes about the dwc:Identification.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.title: Scientific Name
fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.comments: When applied to an Organism or Occurrence, this term should be used to represent the scientific name that was applied to the associated Organism in accordance with the Taxon to which it was or is currently identified. Names should be compliant to the most recent nomenclatural code. For example, names of hybrids for algae, fungi and plants should follow the rules of the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Schenzhen Code Articles H.1, H.2 and H.3). Thus, use the multiplication sign `×` (Unicode `U+00D7`, HTML `×`) to identify a hybrid, not `x` or `X`, if possible.
fields.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet); `×Agropogon littoralis`; `Mentha ×smithiana`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis`
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known. When forming part of a dwc:Identification, this should be the name in lowest level taxonomic rank that can be determined. This term should not contain identification qualifications, which should instead be supplied in the dwc:identificationQualifier term.

fields.name: taxonRank
fields.title: Taxon Rank
fields.description: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Schenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).
fields.rdfs:comment: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.title: Kingdom
fields.description: The full scientific name of the kingdom in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the kingdom in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: phylum
fields.title: Phylum
fields.description: The full scientific name of the phylum or division in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the phylum or division in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: class
fields.title: Class
fields.description: The full scientific name of the class in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the class in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: order
fields.title: Order
fields.description: The full scientific name of the order in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the order in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: family
fields.title: Family
fields.description: The full scientific name of the family in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the family in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: genus
fields.title: Genus
fields.description: The full scientific name of the genus in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the genus in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

fields.name: materialEntityID
fields.title: Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: eventID
fields.title: Event ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: materialCategory
fields.title: Material Category
fields.description: A broad category that best matches the nature of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a limited, tightly controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: materialEntityType
fields.title: Material Entity Type
fields.description: A narrow category that best matches the nature of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: A more generic classification of a dwc:MaterialEntity than dwc:preparations. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `Macro-object`; `Micro-object`; `Oversized object`; `Cut/polished gemstone`; `Compound Specimen`; `Core`; `Mixed Materials`; `Environmental sample`; `Microscope slide`; `Spore print`; `Macrofossil`; `Mesofossil`; `Microfossil`; `Pinned object/specimen`; `Taxidermy mount`; `Blood sampling cards`; `Oversized fossil`; `Anthropogenic Artifact`
fields.rdfs:comment: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: institutionCode
fields.title: Institution Code
fields.description: A name (or acronym) an organization.
fields.rdfs:comment: A name (or acronym) an organization.

fields.name: institutionID
fields.title: Institution ID
fields.description: An identifier for an organization.
fields.comments: For physical specimens, the recommended best practice is to use a globally unique and resolvable identifier from a collections registry such as the Research Organization Registry (ROR) or the Global Registry of Scientific Collections (https://scientific-collections.gbif.org/).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the institution having custody of the object(s) or information referred to in the record.

fields.name: ownerInstitutionCode
fields.title: Owner Institution Code
fields.description: A name (or acronym) in use by an institution having ownership of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.rdfs:comment: The name (or acronym) in use by the institution having ownership of the object(s) or information referred to in the record.

fields.name: ownerInstitutionID
fields.title: Owner Institution ID
fields.description: An identifier for an institution that owns a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: For physical specimens, the recommended best practice is to use a globally unique and resolvable identifier from a collections registry such as the Research Organization Registry (ROR) or the Global Registry of Scientific Collections (https://scientific-collections.gbif.org/).

fields.name: collectionCode
fields.title: Collection Code
fields.description: A name, acronym, coden, or initialism identifying a collection.
fields.rdfs:comment: The name, acronym, coden, or initialism identifying the collection or data set from which the record was derived.

fields.name: catalogNumber
fields.title: Catalog Number
fields.description: An identifier (preferably unique) for a dwc:MaterialEntity within a collection.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier (preferably unique) for the record within the data set or collection.

fields.name: preparations
fields.title: Preparations
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of preparations and preservation methods for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of preparations and preservation methods for a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: disposition
fields.title: Disposition
fields.description: A current state of a dwc:MaterialEntity with respect to where it can be found.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The current state of a dwc:MaterialEntity with respect to a collection.

fields.name: derivedFromMaterialEntityID
fields.title: Derived From Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity from which this dwc:MaterialEntity was derived.
fields.comments: This dwc:MaterialEntity is separate from a dwc:MaterialEntity from which it was derived (cf. dwc:isPartOfMaterialEntityID). Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: materialEntityID
fields.title: Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Values of dwc:materialEntityID are intended to uniquely and persistently identify a particular dwc:MaterialEntity within some context. Examples of context include a particular sample collection, an organization, or the worldwide scale. Recommended best practice is to use a persistent, globally unique identifier. The identifier is bound to a physical object (a dwc:MaterialEntity) as opposed to a particular digital record (representation) of that physical object.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: assertionID
fields.title: Assertion ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Assertion.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: assertionType
fields.title: Assertion Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Assertion.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: assertionValueNumeric
fields.title: Assertion Value Numeric
fields.description: An asserted value, if it is numeric.

fields.name: assertionUnit
fields.title: Assertion Unit
fields.description: Unit associated with the value in dwc:assertionValue or dwc:assertionValueNumeric.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Ontology of Units of Measure http://www.wurvoc.org/vocabularies/om-1.8/ of SI units, derived units, or other non-SI units accepted for use within the SI. For units that are composed of multiple parts, use the patterns as given in "A Primer for Communicating Mathematics via Plain Text" (https://cse.sc.edu/~fenner/latex-ASCII.pdf) by Stephen Fenner (e.g., `g/cm^3` for grams per cubic centimeter). For other units, provide the value as a recognizable standard (e.g., '%') or written out in full and in the plural (e.g., `individuals`). It is fine to provide non-SI units in the original language of the dataset.

fields.name: mediaID
fields.title: Media ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Media resource.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: materialEntityID
fields.title: Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Values of dwc:materialEntityID are intended to uniquely and persistently identify a particular dwc:MaterialEntity within some context. Examples of context include a particular sample collection, an organization, or the worldwide scale. Recommended best practice is to use a persistent, globally unique identifier. The identifier is bound to a physical object (a dwc:MaterialEntity) as opposed to a particular digital record (representation) of that physical object.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: mediaID
fields.title: Media ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Media resource.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: mediaType
fields.title: Media Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Media resource.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: The nature or genre of the resource.

fields.name: description
fields.title: Description
fields.description: An account of the resource.
fields.comments: Description of collection or individual resource, containing the Who, What, When, Where and Why as free-form text. This property optionally allows the presentation of detailed information and will in most cases be shown together with the resource title. If both a description and a caption are present in the metadata, a description is typically displayed instead of the resource, whereas a caption is displayed together with the resource. The description should aim to be a good proxy for the underlying media resource in cases where only text can be shown, whereas the caption may only make sense when shown together with the media. Thus, in HTML it would be appropriate to use dcterms:description values for alt attributes in img elements. Often only one of description or caption is present; choose the term most appropriate for your metadata. It is the role of implementers of an AC concrete representation (e.g., an XML Schema, an RDF representation, etc.) to decide and document how formatting advice will be represented in descriptions serialized according to such representations.
fields.rdfs:comment: An account of the resource.

fields.name: accessURI
fields.title: Access URI
fields.description: A URI that uniquely identifies a service that provides a representation of the underlying resource.
fields.comments: If this resource can be acquired by an http request, its http URL SHOULD be given. If not, but it has some URI in another URI scheme, that MAY be given here. Value might point to something offline, such as a published CD, etc. For example, the doi of a published CD would be a suitable value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A URI that uniquely identifies a service that provides a representation of the underlying resource.

fields.name: format
fields.title: Format
fields.description: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, denoted by a controlled value string.
fields.comments: A controlled value string describing the technical format of the resource (file format or physical medium). The string SHOULD be a controlled value from the Audiovisual Core Controlled Vocabulary for Dublin Core dcterms:format, although it MAY be any Media Type (MIME type) value from the IANA list of Media Types (https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml) or any commonly used file extension string. Human-readable information about the Controlled Vocabulary for format is at http://rs.tdwg.org/ac/doc/format/. This term can be used to describe offline digital content. In cases where the provided Service Access Point URL includes a standard file extension from which the format can be inferred, it is permissible to not provide a value for this property. See also the entry for dcterms:format in the Audiovisual Core term list document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces, https://web.archive.org/web/20171126043657/https://github.com/dcmi/repository/blob/master/mediawiki_wiki/FAQ/DC_and_DCTERMS_Namespaces.md, for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. It is best practice to use dcterms:format instead of dc:format whenever practical. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.
fields.rdfs:comment: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource.

The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters.

fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: materialEntityID
fields.title: Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Values of dwc:materialEntityID are intended to uniquely and persistently identify a particular dwc:MaterialEntity within some context. Examples of context include a particular sample collection, an organization, or the worldwide scale. Recommended best practice is to use a persistent, globally unique identifier. The identifier is bound to a physical object (a dwc:MaterialEntity) as opposed to a particular digital record (representation) of that physical object.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: readCount
fields.title: Read Count
fields.description: A number of reads for a dwc:NucleotideSequence in a dwc:NucleotideAnalysis.

fields.name: totalReadCount
fields.title: Total Read Count
fields.description: A total number of reads in a dwc:NucleotideAnalysis.

fields.name: nucleotideSequenceID
fields.title: Nucleotide Sequence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:NucleotideSequence.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: sequence
fields.title: Sequence
fields.description: A string representing nucleotide base pairs.

fields.name: occurrenceID
fields.title: Occurrence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Occurrence.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the dwc:Occurrence (as opposed to a particular digital record of the dwc:Occurrence). In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one from a combination of identifiers in the record that will most closely make the dwc:occurrenceID globally unique.

fields.name: eventID
fields.title: Event ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: surveyTargetID
fields.title: Survey Target ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: organismQuantity
fields.title: Organism Quantity
fields.description: A number or enumeration value for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.comments: A dwc:organismQuantity must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantityType.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)
fields.rdfs:comment: A number or enumeration value for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.

fields.name: organismQuantityType
fields.title: Organism Quantity Type
fields.description: The type of quantification system used for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.comments: A dwc:organismQuantityType must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantity. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)
fields.rdfs:comment: The type of quantification system used for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.

fields.name: lifeStage
fields.title: Life Stage
fields.description: An age class or life stage of a dwc:Organism.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: The age class or life stage of the dwc:Organism(s) at the time the dwc:Occurrence was recorded.

fields.name: vitality
fields.title: Vitality
fields.description: An indication of whether a dwc:Organism was alive or dead at the time of collection or observation.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: An indication of whether a dwc:Organism was alive or dead at the time of collection or observation.

fields.name: occurrenceStatus
fields.title: Occurrence Status
fields.description: A statement about the detection or non-detection of a dwc:Organism.
fields.comments: For dwc:Occurrences, the default vocabulary is recommended to consist of 'detected' and 'notDetected', but can be extended by implementers with good justification. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A statement about the presence or absence of a dwc:Taxon at a dcterms:Location.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.title: Scientific Name
fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet); `×Agropogon littoralis`; `Mentha ×smithiana`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis`
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known. When forming part of a dwc:Identification, this should be the name in lowest level taxonomic rank that can be determined. This term should not contain identification qualifications, which should instead be supplied in the dwc:identificationQualifier term.

fields.name: taxonRank
fields.title: Taxon Rank
fields.description: A taxonomic rank of the most specific name in a dwc:scientificName.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Schenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).
fields.rdfs:comment: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.

fields.name: surveyID
fields.title: Survey ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Survey.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: eventID
fields.title: Event ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: verbatimSiteDescriptions
fields.title: Verbatim Site Descriptions
fields.description: Original textual description of site(s).
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Wet flatwoods | Wet depression surrounded by mesic longleaf pine flatwoods | Ground cover of thick Andropogon spp., Sporobolus floridanus, Vaccinium spp, Rhynchospora spp., Centella erecta, Panicum rigidulum.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space ( | ).

fields.name: verbatimSiteNames
fields.title: Verbatim Site Names
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `East Coastal Fringe | St. Marks Wildlife Management Area`; `S1 | S2 | C1 | C2 | R14 | R22 | W1`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.

fields.name: reportedWeather
fields.title: Reported Weather
fields.description: A list of weather or climatic conditions present during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a key:value encoding schema for a data interchange format such as JSON.
fields.examples: `flooding during week 3 of surveys`; `rockslide at site 2`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list of weather or climatic conditions present during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: verbatimTargetScope
fields.title: Verbatim Target Scope
fields.description: A verbatim original description of a dwc:Event scope.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is first to populate explicit scope terms to the fullest extent possible (e.g., eco:targetTaxonomicScope). It is not recommended to use this term in assessing absence or completeness.
fields.rdfs:comment: The verbatim original description of the dwc:Event scope.

fields.name: protocolNames
fields.title: Protocol Names
fields.description: Categorical descriptive names for the dwc:Protocols used during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary and separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: Categorical descriptive names for the methods used during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: protocolDescriptions
fields.title: Protocol Descriptions
fields.description: A detailed description of the dwc:Protocols used during a dwc:Survey.
fields.comments: This description should be associated with protocols provided in eco:protocolNames. The description may include deviations from a protocol referred to in eco:protocolReferences. Recommended good practice is to provide information about instruments used, calibration, etc. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Three conventional harp traps (3.2m ht x 2.2m w) were established in flight path zones for a period of 4 hrs at dawn and dusk for a total of 10 trap nights. Traps were visited on an hourly basis during each deployment period and the trap catch recorded for species, size, weight, sex, age and maternal status.`
fields.rdfs:comment: A detailed description of the methods used during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: protocolReferences
fields.title: Protocol References
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of dcterms:BibliographicResources used in a dwc:Protocol.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Penguins from space: faecal stains reveal the location of emperor penguin colonies, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00467.x`
fields.rdfs:comment: The references to the methods used during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: isAbundanceReported
fields.title: Is Abundance Reported
fields.description: The number of dwc:Organisms collected or observed was reported.
fields.comments: Typically the abundance values would be reported in a dwc:organismQuantity and dwc:organismQuantityType terms for the child dwc:Occurrence records for this dwc:Event.
fields.rdfs:comment: The number of dwc:Organisms collected or observed was reported.

fields.name: hasMaterialSamples
fields.title: Has Material Samples
fields.description: Material samples were collected during a dwc:Event.
fields.rdfs:comment: Material samples were collected during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: materialSampleTypes
fields.title: Material Sample Types
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of material sample types collected during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary and separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of material sample types collected during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: samplingPerformedBy
fields.title: Sampling Performed By
fields.description: A dcterms:Agent responsible for sampling.
fields.comments: The sampling dwc:Event could be at any level of hierarchy. In the case of a higher level (parent) dwc:Event, include all the organizations or people involved in the child dwc:Events that contributed to the parent dwc:Event. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `North American Butterfly Association`; `KK Wall`; `JJ Green`; `LL Pink and FF Grey | Aspen Center for Environmental Studies`
fields.rdfs:comment: A person, group, or organization responsible for recording the dwc:Event.

fields.name: isSamplingEffortReported
fields.title: Is Sampling Effort Reported
fields.description: The sampling effort associated with a dwc:Event was reported.
fields.comments: Typically values of effort would be captured under the terms eco:samplingEffortValue and eco:samplingEffortUnit.
fields.rdfs:comment: The sampling effort associated with the dwc:Event was reported.

fields.name: surveyTargetID
fields.title: Survey Target ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier. Note: values of this term are not meant to be unique within a dwc:SurveyTarget. A full dwc:SurveyTarget is composed of all records that share the same dwc:surveyTargetID.

fields.name: surveyID
fields.title: Survey ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Survey.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: surveyTargetType
fields.title: Survey Target Type
fields.description: A scope a dwc:SurveyTarget describes.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetValue
fields.title: Survey Target Value
fields.description: A value of a characteristic to include or exclude in a dwc:SurveyTarget for a given dwc:surveyTargetType.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: includeOrExclude
fields.title: Include Or Exclude
fields.description: Whether the combination of dwc:surveyTargetType and dwc:surveyTargetValue is included or excluded in a dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Combinations of dwc:SurveyTarget records of inclusions and exclusions can define complex scopes such as all flying adult Aves except Passeriformes. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary consisting of 'include' and 'exclude' only.

fields.name: isSurveyTargetFullyReported
fields.title: Is Survey Target Fully Reported
fields.description: A declaration of whether the counts for an instance of the dwc:SurveyTarget report everything that matches the declared dwc:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: If true (the survey target is fully reported - nothing was left unreported), then this enables inference of absence of detection for everything in that dwc:SurveyTarget that is included but that does not appear in the counts (absent counts signify absence of detection).

fields.name: usagePolicyID
fields.title: Usage Policy ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:UsagePolicy.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: rights
fields.title: Rights
fields.description: Information about rights held in and over the resource. A full-text, readable copyright statement, as required by the national legislation of the copyright holder. On collections, this applies to all contained objects, unless the object itself has a different statement. Examples: “Copyright XY 2008, all rights reserved”, “© 2008 XY Museum” , `Public Domain.`; `Copyright unknown.` Do not place just the name of the copyright holder(s) here! That belongs in a list in the xmpRights:Owner field, which should be supplied if dc:rights is not 'Public Domain', which is appropriate only if the resource is known to be not under copyright. See also the entry for dcterms:rights in this document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.
fields.examples: `Copyright 2014 Ron Thomas` or a URI like `http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode`
fields.rdfs:comment: Information about rights held in and over the resource. A full-text, readable copyright statement, as required by the national legislation of the copyright holder. On collections, this applies to all contained objects, unless the object itself has a different statement. Examples: “Copyright XY 2008, all rights reserved”, “© 2008 XY Museum” , `Public Domain.`; `Copyright unknown.` Do not place just the name of the copyright holder(s) here! That belongs in a list in the xmpRights:Owner field, which should be supplied if dc:rights is not 'Public Domain', which is appropriate only if the resource is known to be not under copyright. See also the entry for dcterms:rights in this document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.

fields.name: owner
fields.title: Owner
fields.description: A name of a dcterms:Agent that owns the copyright for a resource.
fields.comments: `unknown`
fields.examples: `The names of the owners `Ron Thomas, Roz Thomas` or a URI that identifies the owner`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list of the names of the owners of the copyright. 'Unknown' is an acceptable value, but 'Public Domain' is not.
